chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Bukeyr, and Jameel Bin Darraj, and Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorced woman becomes irrevocably divorced (bayna'nah) at the first drop of the third menstruation.
He said: I said, 'It has reached me that Rabi'ah al-Ra'y said, 'She becomes irrevocably divorced at the first drop.'
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He lied. It is not from his opinion. Rather, it is something that reached him from Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.تَبِينُ: She becomes irrevocably divorced (bayna'nah), meaning the revocable phase ends and she is fully separated until remarriage
key_terms.رَبِيعَةَ الرَّأْيِ: Rabi'ah al-Ra'y, a prominent jurist known for his independent reasoning

ai.seo_question: When does a woman become irrevocably divorced after a triple divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise moment of irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in) for a woman in her iddah, establishing that the separation occurs at the first drop of blood from the third menstruation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the attribution of this ruling to Rabi'ah al-Ra'y, distinguishing between independent juristic reasoning and a transmitted tradition from Imam Ali (AS), thereby highlighting the importance of source verification in Shia fiqh. This distinction underscores the scholarly rigor in attributing legal principles to their original divine or prophetic sources rather than later juristic interpretations.
